fomc-2026-10.standing: The Federal Reserve's rate-setting committee, which meets eight times a year to set the overnight rate US banks lend at. Its decisions price dollar borrowing worldwide, from American mortgages to emerging-market debt.
fomc-2026-10.recent: Gasoline lifted US inflation to 3.7% in September, and Warsh has called AI a shock to the economy while withholding guidance on the next move. This meeting settles how the committee weighs an energy-driven price rise against that shock, and whether Warsh's vow of price stability comes with any signal on where rates go.

ecb-2026-10.standing: The European Central Bank's Governing Council, which meets eight times a year to set interest rates for the countries sharing the euro. Its deposit rate drives borrowing costs for some 350 million people, and the euro moves with it.
ecb-2026-10.recent: Euro-area households now expect 3.1% inflation, up from 3%, which is the drift the European Central Bank guards against. Lagarde has credited the French bond selloff with tightening conditions, and economists already point to December for a hike. This meeting settles how the council reads that signal, and how it weighs France's rising borrowing costs.

boj-2026-10.standing: The Bank of Japan's policy board, which meets eight times a year to set the country's short-term interest rate. Its decisions move the yen and the yield on Japanese government debt, and reach borrowers far beyond Japan.
boj-2026-10.recent: Yen-priced imports cost 24.5% more than a year ago and wholesale inflation has reached 6.8%, the bill for a weak yen landing in Japan's prices. The board's question is whether that is an import shock it can look past, or the wage-driven inflation Tokyo has been waiting for, now taking hold behind it.

boe-2026-11.standing: The Bank of England's Monetary Policy Committee, nine members who vote eight times a year on Bank Rate. Their decision sets the price of UK mortgages and business loans, and sterling and gilt yields move with it.
boe-2026-11.recent: This decision lands after inflation and borrowing data that sharpened the chancellor's Budget challenge, so the committee sets rates for a government with little room of its own. Iran threats have kept oil in play, reopening the argument over whether a central bank hikes into an energy shock or looks through it.

fomc-2026-12.standing: The Federal Reserve's rate-setting committee, which meets eight times a year to set the overnight rate US banks lend at. Its decisions price dollar borrowing worldwide, from American mortgages to emerging-market debt.
fomc-2026-12.recent: September's 3.7% inflation, lifted by gasoline, has revived bets on a Fed hike, while Warsh has called AI a shock to the economy and vowed price stability without giving guidance. The meeting settles whether a gasoline-led price rise is what this committee fights, or whether Warsh's AI shock changes what price stability asks of it.

g20-2026-miami.standing: The annual meeting of leaders of the world's largest economies, hosted by the member holding the rotating presidency. Its members produce about 85% of global output, and its communiqué sets shared lines on trade and debt.
g20-2026-miami.recent: The Miami summit opens with its guest list in dispute: Merz has urged Trump to invite South Africa. Zelenskyy is eyeing a meeting with the US and Russia on its margins, as Putin pushes a three-way summit with Trump and Xi. And the Emissions Gap Report has just named the United States the G20's outlier on climate.

ecb-2026-12.standing: The European Central Bank's Governing Council, which meets eight times a year to set interest rates for the countries sharing the euro. Its deposit rate drives borrowing costs for some 350 million people, and the euro moves with it.
ecb-2026-12.recent: Euro-area households now expect 3.1% inflation, up from 3%, and the ECB meets in December after a pause with that drift on the table. Its other weight is France: a bond rout has already raised borrowing costs there, and Lagarde has credited the selloff, so the council decides how much of the job the market has already done.

boe-2026-12.standing: The Bank of England's Monetary Policy Committee, nine members who vote eight times a year on Bank Rate. Their decision sets the price of UK mortgages and business loans, and sterling and gilt yields move with it.
boe-2026-12.recent: The committee meets with the chancellor's Budget squeezed by the same inflation and borrowing data it is weighing. With oil wavering on Iran threats, the open question is whether a central bank should hike into an energy shock or look through it, and this decision settles which reading the Bank of England takes.

boj-2026-12.standing: The Bank of Japan's policy board, which meets eight times a year to set the country's short-term interest rate. Its decisions move the yen and the yield on Japanese government debt, and reach borrowers far beyond Japan.
boj-2026-12.recent: Yen-priced imports cost 24.5% more than a year ago, and Japan's debate has turned to whether wage-driven inflation is taking over from the import bill. The board decides how far to lean against that while the yen trades as a safe haven, and every swing in it feeds straight back into what Japan pays for imports.

fred-us-pce-2026-10-29.standing: The Bureau of Economic Analysis's monthly report on personal income and spending, carrying the PCE price index the Federal Reserve targets at 2%. It moves rate expectations, Treasury yields and the dollar.
fred-us-pce-2026-10-29.recent: The Bureau of Economic Analysis publishes the next reading of US PCE prices alongside household income and spending. It settles how fast prices rose over the month it covers, which is the figure the inflation target is measured against.

fred-us-gdp-2026-10-29.standing: The Bureau of Economic Analysis's quarterly estimate of US gross domestic product, first published about a month after each quarter ends and revised twice after. Treasury yields, the dollar and Fed expectations move on it.
fred-us-gdp-2026-10-29.recent: The Bureau of Economic Analysis publishes its estimate of how fast US GDP grew over the quarter. The release settles the growth rate, and which parts of spending carried it.
